From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Silva <rachel.silva@embertech.com>
Date: 2027-05-20 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: QBR prep: EmberTech — health snapshot, renewal risk register & exec asks

Team — attaching the health snapshot and the working renewal risk register for EmberTech's upcoming QBR (see attachments). Quick summary up top:

- Current usage: steady but 18% below committed footprint (mainly non-prod).
- Latency spikes: 2 incidents in last 30 days tied to model alpha rollouts (root cause: caching misconfiguration).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence in progress; customer asked for audit timeline during procurement.
- Financial: renewal target: $420k ARR; customer is evaluating a 10% price increase request.

Primary asks:
1) Exec presence: Grace — can you join the bridge for the customer QBR on 2027-05-26 11:00 PT? They want a short leadership review if we surface an SLA credit discussion.
2) Pricing stance: Marissa — summarize concessions we've already approved and your recommended negotiation boundary.
3) Tech mitigation: Karthik — give a 3-bullet mitigation plan for the latency incidents and ETA to stabilize.

I've flagged 4 renewal risk lines in the attached register (columns: risk, severity, owner, mitigation, eta). Please reply inline with updates by EOD today so I can finalize the exec brief for Friday.

Thanks —
Sergio
Director, Customer Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ember_qbr_health_snapshot.xlsx (summary + charts), renewal-risk-register.csv

Thanks, Sergio — quick updates inline.

- Pricing/concessions: We already committed a 5% marketing credit for onboarding issues earlier this year and offered a one-time training package (no monetary reduction). Procurement pushed back on the 10% list increase; they want to see SLA remediation before discussing price. My recommended negotiation boundary: cap additional concessions to 3% on list plus a 6-month staged rollout of quoted price. Owner: Marissa.

- Commercial risk: Customer procurement is circulating a tight approval window (decision target: 2027-06-15). If we need more time, they may require a shorter contract term.

- Suggested next step: If Grace can join the bridge, we should open with a 10-minute leadership summary, then move to joint remediation commitments.

Also added comments to renewal-risk-register.csv: marked 'procurement pressure' as High and set proposed mitigation to 'exec bridge + concession cap'.

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-20 11:27:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: EmberTech — health snapshot, renewal risk register & exec asks

Sergio / Marissa — technical summary and mitigations:

1) Root cause recap: The two latency spikes were triggered after we pushed model-alpha-v3 to non-production clusters without the prefix KV-cache enabled for a subset of prefix-heavy calls. This caused cache misses and CPU fallback on a small percentage (~4%) of token streams.

2) Short-term mitigation (by 2027-05-21 EOD): re-enable prefix KV-cache and rollback alpha-v3 on non-prod; add a targeted rate-limiter for prefix-heavy routes.  Estimated impact: reduce spike probability by ~90%.

3) Medium-term (2 weeks): add a preflight canary with traffic shaping and observability hooks to catch the cache-mismatch before rollout.

4) Long-term (quarter): expand automatic prefix detection and improve default caching heuristics; include guardrails in our model onboarding playbook.

I've also updated renewal-risk-register.csv: added 'technical stabilization ETA' to the latency risk line with 2027-05-21 for short-term and 2027-06-04 for medium-term. Happy to walk through a short tech slide during the bridge.

—Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the succinct packet. I can join the bridge on 2027-05-26 11:00 PT for a 10–15 minute leadership segment. A few points from me:

- Authorization: I'm prepared to confirm a leadership-level goodwill gesture (up to 3% one-time credit) contingent on Karthik's short-term mitigation being validated post-bridge. We should make clear that any ongoing credits require additional remediation commitments.
- Messaging: We should lead with the positive: product stability for core routes is solid, and the incidents affected an isolated non-prod path. Then present the concrete mitigations and timeline.
- Ask for the customer: request a 30-day decision window extension to 2027-07-15 to avoid pressure-induced concessioning; frame it as collaborative risk-reduction time.

Sergio — please finalize the exec brief and include the 3% cap and the 30-day extension request as options. I will be on the bridge and can speak to escalation and goodwill policy.

—Grace
VP, Customer Experience
Redwood Inference

- Availability: I can confirm the 2027-05-26 11:00 PT slot for the QBR. We'll have our CTO and head of procurement on the call.
